subject.declared_domain: The ontology rail sitting between C2 and C3: the OBLIGATION a motif or system carries -- delivery cadence, completeness-over-a-scope, canonical source, layer grammar -- plus the lifecycle axis that types how a contracted thing behaves over time. It is the INTENT half of intent-denominator synchronization, sourced from ABOVE the artifact. This card covers the rail's definition, its declaration instances, and its validator. It does NOT cover C3.i-as-built, which is 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~X's subject (SC-d-*).

methodology.how: A hand-authored static YAML block in the ontology rule bank -- at 13 keys the largest of the three D-rails -- resolved BY HOME like its siblings. It COMPOSES pre-existing estate obligations (PSTMRT's completeness axis, TRIGGER_LAYER doctrine, the written MDPF delivery-cadence contract, and keep-dormant.yaml's four DORMANT fields, adopted verbatim with one strengthening). It INVENTS the obligation TYPE vocabulary, the contract_record shape, the lifecycle_class enum and its polarity table, and the sibling lifecycle_stage axis. UNLIKE D1 AND D2, THIS RAIL HAS BOTH AN INSTANCE STORE AND AN EXECUTABLE VALIDATOR: declarations live as YAML records and .tools/contract_declare_lint.py checks them. The validator is a LEXICAL floor only -- it resolves enum tokens against the bank and says so on its own face.

key.identity_space: Subject keys are free-form YAML mapping keys inside each per-subject contract file (e.g. a pipeline or artifact name), joined to governance sources by the intent_source POINTER. Across carriers there are three distinct identity spaces -- canon-plane record keys, Iceberg graph_contracts value-surface keys, and C7 influence-closure Git-plane ids.
key.declared_mapping: PARTIAL, and unusually good by estate standards on one half while absent on the other. DECLARED: the existence and distinctness of the three carriers is stated at SYSTEM_DEFINITIONS.yaml:478, with the explicit rule that 'a consumer names which it reads'. NOT DECLARED: any mapping BETWEEN the three id spaces. Nothing states whether a subject key in carrier 1 denotes the same resource as a row in carrier 2 or 3, so the three populations cannot be joined, deduplicated, or reconciled by any mechanical means.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: The validator returns a TYPED, LOUD, well-formed rejection on stdout naming the offending field, the illegal value and the ratified set -- and it returns rc=0 while doing so. Verdict and exit code disagree BY DESIGN and the source says why. The rail's own declaration-level failure rule is separate and also loud: a missing or unresolvable required field renders the declaration UNKNOWN, LOUD, with no fallback to the declared value and no fallback to PERMANENT.
silent_degrade_paths: AN rc-ONLY CONSUMER CANNOT DISTINGUISH PASS FROM REJECT -- both exit 0. A gate wired to this validator's exit code fails OPEN, and the source names this hazard explicitly rather than leaving it to be discovered.
the lint is a LEXICAL floor: a record whose tokens all resolve but whose meaning has drifted (A7.3) passes silently, and the tool prints that it is not clearance.
the `describes` field is deliberately un-lintable, and a PASS is explicitly silent about it.
6 of 14 records carry zero obligations -- UNDECLARED by the rail's own definition -- and the validator passes them without comment.
revalidate_by's shape is unchecked, so 'on produce' on 14 of 14 records passes while leaving the decay control with no evaluable window.
failure_mode.evidence: ⛔ EXERCISED WITH BOTH ARMS REACHABLE FROM DIFFERENT TRUTHS, not read off a docstring. ARM 1 (real declaration): python .tools/contract_declare_lint.py org/modules/graph/estate-contracts/mdpf.contracts.yaml -> '== PIN(none) == records=7 findings=0 / == HEAD == records=7 findings=0 / VERDICT: PASS', rc=0. ARM 2 (a planted mutant -- one record carrying lifecycle_class 'ZZZ_NO_SUCH_CLASS_9999' and locality 'ZZZ_NO_SUCH_LOCALITY_9999', authored to a scratch file so no carded surface was touched): -> 'records=1 findings=2', with both REJECT lines naming the field, the illegal value and the ratified set, then 'VERDICT: REJECT' -- and rc=0. The two arms return DIFFERENT stdout from DIFFERENT truths, so distinguishable_from_true_negative is 'yes' ON STDOUT, which is the plane the tool designates as authoritative. IT IS 'no' ON rc, AND rc IS THE PLANE A NAIVE CALLER READS. The source states the reason at .tools/contract_declare_lint.py:232-238 @423d61cade: 'THE VERDICT IS CARRIED IN STDOUT, NOT IN rc. This host has a DOCUMENTED rc-corruption class ... A GATE whose verdict rides only on an exit code FAILS OPEN wherever that code is corrupted -- and a gate that fails open is worse than no gate, because it is believed.' So this is a DELIBERATE, DOCUMENTED design choice against a real host defect, not an oversight -- and it is nonetheless a live trap for any consumer that wires this tool to a gate by exit code. Declaration-level UNKNOWN-LOUD rule at org/modules/graph/NFRA_ONTOLOGY_RULE_BANK.yaml:606-607 @5fc45ad69d (required_field_failure: 'a MISSING or UNRESOLVABLE required field renders the declaration UNKNOWN, LOUD ... it does NOT fall back to the declared value, and it does NOT fall back to PERMANENT').
failure_mode.owner: 1.0.0_SA_CTO for the validator's rc/stdout contract; 4.0.0_SA_CRO for the declaration-level failure rules

verdict.why: D3 is the most substantial of the three rails and the only one with all three of a definition, an instance store and a working validator -- so the TO's and PRD's expectation that it would card EMPTY is falsified by measurement, and that falsification is this card's primary result. It is genuinely standable: the definition is 13 keys deep, 14 records are landed and validate, and the validator's failure path is loud and typed with both arms exercised from different truths. It is QUALIFIED rather than SOUND because four defects bind a consumer, each with its own owner and clock: (1) one rail carries THREE distinct carrier populations on three planes with the multiplicity declared but NO MAPPING between the id spaces, so the populations cannot be reconciled mechanically; (2) 6 of 14 landed records carry zero obligations, which the rail's own text defines as UNDECLARED, while passing the lint cleanly; (3) all 14 records carry a revalidate_by that is a condition rather than a dated window, leaving the decay control -- which the rail itself calls the difference between a revalidation and a ritual -- with nothing to evaluate; (4) the validator's REJECT and PASS both exit 0, so any consumer gating on rc fails open, a hazard the source documents deliberately and which is real regardless. It is not UNSOUND: every one of these is bounded, named, and leaves the rail usable by a consumer who knows about them. NOT INCOMPLETE: all 7 rows are worked and carry measured bases, including the two rows where the honest answer was 'unmeasured by this lane' -- those name the instruments tried and why each could not answer, rather than being left blank. Per QUALIFY-DO-NOT-FIX this lane remediated nothing: no rail, record, validator or registry was edited, and the planted mutant was written to a scratch path outside the repo.
blocking_defects: For any consumer joining or reconciling D3 populations: three carriers exist on three planes with no declared mapping between their id spaces. Name which carrier you read; do not assume a subject in one is the subject in another. Owner UNOWNED.

For any consumer treating the landed population as contracted: 6 of 14 records carry zero obligations and are UNDECLARED by the rail's own definition, while passing the lint. Owner 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~D.

For any consumer relying on decay/staleness: revalidate_by is 'on produce' on 14 of 14 records -- a condition, not a window -- and its shape is unchecked by the validator. Owners 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps~D and 4.0.0_SA_CRO.
For any gate wired to contract_declare_lint.py: REJECT and PASS both return rc=0. Score the STDOUT verdict, never the exit code. Owner 1.0.0_SA_CTO.
